# Correction: direct endpoint recovery by a classical maximum principle

4 November 2026. This corrects the significance and acquisition mechanism of the earlier blind stationary tomography packet. Its theorem remains valid, but its graphic-matroid reconstruction is unnecessary. A simpler same-data operation also weakens the sufficient graph assumption from 3-vertex-connectivity to biconnectivity. The maximum principle itself is established mathematics, with directly relevant stationary-response prior below. No priority claim is made for its inverse-problem application.

## 1. Exact operation and proof

Use the column convention for an irreducible finite Markov generator W: off-diagonal entries are nonnegative, 1ᵀW=0, and Wπ=0 with π>0. An intervention changes only the two directed rates on {a,b}; symmetric multiplication of those rates by an unknown positive factor is a special case. Let π′ be its stationary distribution and d=π′−π. Assume d≠0. Subtracting stationarity gives

W d = α(e_b−e_a), with α≠0.

Define h_i=d_i/π_i and L=W diag(π). Since L1=0, at every state i,

(Lh)_i = Σ_(j≠i) W_ij π_j (h_j−h_i).

Thus h is harmonic at every nontarget state. Assume, for this pair, that the baseline positive-rate support contains a spanning bidirected graph which remains connected after deleting either a or b. A spanning biconnected bidirected graph suffices simultaneously for every target pair.

Reverse the names a,b if necessary so α>0. At b the displayed sum is positive, so b cannot maximize h. At a it is negative, so a cannot minimize h. If a nontarget i maximized h, its harmonic equation, a sum of nonpositive terms with positive coefficients along bidirected edges, would force every neighboring value to equal that maximum. Propagate along a path from i to b avoiding a. All internal vertices are nontargets, so b would also maximize h, a contradiction. The analogous argument along a path avoiding b excludes a nontarget minimum. Hence

argmax_i h_i = a, and argmin_i h_i = b,

uniquely. Their unordered pair is the intervention target, regardless of its unknown amplitude or sign. Computing π′_i/π_i gives exactly the same extrema. This uses the measured state names directly and needs no graph reconstruction or row-permutation alignment.

This auditor also read and verified CORRECTION.md, SHA256 80b7fc407d2487a83b459f5eaf028b9cf31156a0d1575b69f08cefd1d5962407. Its algebra, biconnected scope, finite symmetric-factor compatibility test, and conservative ratio-error bound B=2 eta/r+2 eta/r^2 for eta<r/2 are correct. Its endpoint-gap requirement g>2B is sufficient; arithmetic error must be included as stated.

**Verdict:** The direct maximum-principle reconstruction is correct. I independently approve the spanning biconnected extension of the exact generator-identification theorem. The earlier three-connected theorem remains true, but graphic reconstruction and state-label alignment are unnecessary. The endpoint principle has direct published prior; this correction should reduce, not inflate, the novelty assessment.

## Independent derivation

For a nonzero finite response d=pi'−pi on an unknown pair {a,b}, stationarity gives Wd=alpha(e_b−e_a), with alpha nonzero. Put h_i=d_i/pi_i and L=W diag(pi). Since Wpi=0, L has zero row sums and nonnegative off-diagonal entries. At every nontarget state,

0 = sum_{j != i} W_ij pi_j (h_j−h_i).

Thus h is harmonic off the target pair. Assume alpha>0. State b cannot be a maximum because (Lh)_b>0; state a cannot be a minimum because (Lh)_a<0. Irreducibility and propagation of equality in the harmonic equation place a at a maximum and b at a minimum.

If the baseline contains a spanning bidirected biconnected selected graph, any nontarget state has a path to b avoiding a. A nontarget maximum would propagate along this path, forcing b to be a maximum, contradiction. Similarly no nontarget can share b's minimum. For alpha<0, the endpoint roles reverse. Therefore the unique maximum and minimum of d_i/pi_i identify the unordered physical target pair in a linear scan. Extra positive directed rates do not spoil the argument.

With those endpoints known, solve 1^T K=0, Kpi=0, and require Kd_e to vanish outside each recovered pair. A spanning biconnected graph has connected cycle matroid. # Independent audit addendum: direct endpoint recovery supersedes graphic reconstruction

2026-11-04. Auditor: independent constructor. This addendum concerns the frozen PROOF.md with SHA256 fb5d4f943cf79c863019eb820f57f5c13683f1b6adc2b683f5c12fb6bab20314. It does not modify that file.

## Finding

The author's newly identified maximum-principle baseline is correct. It removes the graphic-matroid reconstruction and positivity-based state-alignment stages entirely. The original exact theorem remains true, but those stages are unnecessary for its stated observation model. Moreover, a spanning biconnected selected graph suffices for full reconstruction. This materially changes the assessment of the construction's leverage and its comparison with existing methods; it is not evidence that the original theorem is false.

## Direct proof

Use the column-generator convention, W pi=0, pi_i>0. For a nonzero response d=pi'−pi on an unknown pair {a,b}, the original finite-response identity is

W d = alpha(e_b−e_a), alpha != 0.

Set h_i=d_i/pi_i and L=W diag(pi). Because W pi=0, L has zero row sums. For each i outside {a,b},

0=(Lh)_i=sum_{j != i} W_ij pi_j (h_j−h_i).

Thus h_i is a positive weighted average of its predecessor values in the baseline graph. The division by pi is essential; extrema of d itself need not identify the pair.

Without loss of generality alpha>0. At any maximum of h, (Lh)_i<=0, so b cannot be a maximum; at any minimum, (Lh)_i>=0, so a cannot be a minimum. A nonterminal maximum propagates along predecessor edges until it reaches a terminal; irreducibility therefore places a at a maximum and b at a minimum.

Now use the spanning bidirected biconnected selected support. If a nontarget i shared the maximum with a, there is a path in this selected graph from i to b avoiding a. Along that path, at every nontarget maximum the harmonic equation forces every positive-weight neighbor also to equal that maximum. Consequently b would attain the maximum, contradiction. Therefore a is the unique maximum. Deleting b and applying the same argument proves b is the unique minimum. For alpha<0 the roles reverse.

Accordingly the unordered pair is exactly {argmax_i h_i, argmin_i h_i}. It takes a linear scan per response. Extra unperturbed directed edges merely add nonnegative averaging weights and do not invalidate the proof.
